# PREAMBLE

> South Africa’s global and local data. Live results of the 4 November 2026 local government elections, a ward-by-ward map, the mayors of the eight metros, and a Coalitions Tracker that groups reporting on the coalition talks into stories with summaries and links to every original article. Updated 26 November 2026, 18:12 SAST.

Data: Independent Electoral Commission (IEC). Summaries are written by Preamble with AI from published reporting; the journalists and politicians quoted do not write for Preamble.

## Main pages

- [2026 election results](https://preamble.co.za/): national vote, ward map and who won each metro
- [Coalitions Tracker](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions.html): every story on the coalition talks, in South Africa and abroad
- [Mayors](https://preamble.co.za/mayors.html): who leads each metro, and who is tipped where talks continue
- [Ward map](https://preamble.co.za/map.html): results for every ward, searchable by address
- [News Tracker (beta)](https://preamble.co.za/news-tracker.html): an animated map of how the coalition stories spread across outlets and voices, day by day

## Coalition stories (newest first)

- [MK’s Nomathamsanqa Mthembu becomes uMhlathuze mayor as the ANC, DA and IFP take KwaDukuza](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/kzn-councils.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): IOL, News24 and SABC News report the MK Party’s Nomathamsanqa Mthembu has been elected uMhlathuze mayor, with News24 saying an ANC-MK pact sidelined the IFP and DA. In KwaDukuza, The Citizen reports a last-minute deal has put the ANC, DA and IFP in control, and Central News South Africa reports the ANC and MK have taken uPhongolo.
- [The EFF wins its first mayoralty in Lekwa-Teemane as a Madibeng plan sidelines the ANC and ActionSA](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/north-west-councils.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): Newsnote and Central News South Africa report the EFF’s Justice Dabampe has taken charge of Lekwa-Teemane Municipality, giving the party its first-ever mayoralty. The Citizen reports the ANC and ActionSA face exclusion from a Madibeng leadership plan.
- [MK members dispute the party’s PR councillor lists and candidates](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/mk-pr-lists.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): The Witness and IOL report the MK Party faces internal discontent and a backlash over its KwaZulu-Natal proportional representation list, and Inside Politic reports MK structures are clashing over a KwaZulu-Natal mayoral candidate. The Daily Dispatch reports the party’s Port St Johns branch is threatening court action over a contested PR councillor list.
- [The ANC leaves coalition choices to its provinces and regions](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/anc-regions.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): EWN and Dan Corder report the ANC’s NEC has let provinces and regions decide coalitions, affecting over 100 hung councils, and SABC News reports the NEC resolved that DA coalitions should be a last resort. IOL and The Common Sense report the ANC has moved Fikile Mbalula’s coalition briefing to Friday, ahead of crucial Gauteng mayoral votes.
- [The DA is shut out of Theewaterskloof and Laingsburg as Western Cape councils pick partners](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/western-cape.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): News24 reports the ANC joined other parties to take control of Theewaterskloof, and IOL and the Cape Times report ActionSA formed a Laingsburg coalition with the PA and ANC, leaving the DA out. IOL reports a three-party agreement puts the DA in line to govern Knysna, and SABC News reports Matzikama council will sit on Thursday after a deadlock over an EFF councillor.
- [Ekurhuleni’s mayoral election moves to Friday as parties wait on the ANC to sign](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/ekurhuleni.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): Ekurhuleni’s new council held its inaugural meeting on 25 November, but the election of a mayor and speaker was postponed, and SABC News, The National and Inside Metros report the vote will take place on Friday. EWN, The National and Sunday World report parties are waiting on the ANC to sign off the coalition deal, and Newsnote reports Herman Mashaba blamed ANC delays for the stalled talks.
- [Malema awaits judgment in his bid to gag Zille over her Joburg claims](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/malema-zille-court.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): EFF leader Julius Malema went to court to stop DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille repeating claims about him, in a dispute linked to the Johannesburg coalition fight, and the court reserved judgment. Zille refused to retract, and Michael Beaumont has challenged her claims, while Central News South Africa reports Glynnis Breytenbach confirmed recommending Shadrack Sibiya to Herman Mashaba in 2016.
- [Faku returns in Buffalo City with the EFF as a DA-led coalition signs for Nelson Mandela Bay](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/eastern-cape-metros.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): Princess Faku was re-elected Buffalo City mayor, beating the UDM’s Nqabayomzi Kwankwa, and BusinessTech reports the ANC teamed up with the EFF. In Nelson Mandela Bay, a DA-led multiparty coalition has been formed, but News24 reports an ANC-led filibuster blocked the vote for mayor and speaker.
- [eThekwini council will reconvene on Friday to elect a mayor and speaker](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/ethekwini.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): eThekwini’s inaugural council meeting adjourned on 24 November without electing a mayor, deputy mayor or speaker, and IOL and DailyNews report the council will reconvene on Friday to do so. IOL reports party sources linking the adjournment to coalition posts, and IOL and Briefly News report the ANC and MK have reached an eThekwini agreement.
- [Will the coalition fights break the national unity government?](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/gnu.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): Adriaan Basson first expected the DA and ANC to copy their national partnership in the councils. By mid-November he was warning that the fight over the cities could bring it down.
- [ActionSA’s condition for any deal: Moya stays in Tshwane](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/tshwane.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): ActionSA made keeping Nasiphi Moya as Tshwane mayor a condition for any coalition, and News24’s Adriaan Basson expected her back.
- [ActionSA bargains with both big parties, then leans towards the ANC](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/actionsa.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): ActionSA’s chair Michael Beaumont spent November talking to both the DA and the ANC, arguing that coalitions, not vote share, decide who governs.
- [MK talks to everyone, the DA included, but says it wants like-minded partners](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/mk.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): MK came third nationally and leads many KwaZulu-Natal councils. Its negotiator Dali Mpofu has met the DA for the first time while warning the ANC about the partners it chooses.
- [In public, Ramaphosa asks for good faith. In private, insiders say he wants the DA kept out of Joburg](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/ramaphosa.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): The president told all parties to bargain in good faith and form councils quickly. A report based on unnamed insiders says he steered the ANC away from the DA in Johannesburg, which the ANC denies.
- [Outside the metros, councils start to pick partners, and Limpopo’s ANC turns to the DA](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/councils.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): With deadlines close, deals are being struck in smaller councils. In Limpopo, the ANC chose the DA over a left-wing bloc, while the IFP expects to seal its KwaZulu-Natal deals this weekend.
- [Joburg will elect its mayor on Friday as parties finish their deal](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/johannesburg.html) (South Africa, updated 26 November 2026): All 270 councillors were sworn in on Monday, but the election of a mayor, deputy mayor and speaker now waits until Friday, 27 November. The ANC, ActionSA, EFF and MK deal that would make Mashaba mayor is in its final stages but still to be signed.
- [‘Privatisation is meant for the poor’: Helen Zille defends DA's plans, cites Cape Town example](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/auto-cape-town.html) (South Africa, updated 25 November 2026): 3 outlets are reporting on the coalition talks in Cape Town. Preamble’s editors have not yet summarised this story; the latest reports are listed below.
- [MK Party promises stable eThekwini government](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/auto-ethekwini.html) (South Africa, updated 25 November 2026): 3 outlets are reporting on the coalition talks in eThekwini. Preamble’s editors have not yet summarised this story; the latest reports are listed below.
- [The ANC loses its grip on South Africa’s metros](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/anc-metros.html) (South Africa, updated 25 November 2026): News24’s columnists saw the ANC’s decline speeding up, and after the count it was left without control of a single metro.
- [Should one deal settle all eight metros?](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/grand-deal.html) (South Africa, updated 25 November 2026): Instead of eight separate fights, Sizwe Mpofu-Walsh floated a single bargain between the DA, ANC and ActionSA over the metro mayors. Others have pitched their own national formulas.
- [The DA offers the ANC 93 mayoralties; ActionSA rejects its Gauteng deal](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/da-offer.html) (South Africa, updated 25 November 2026): The DA’s nationwide framework would have the ANC lead 93 hung councils, the DA 24 and the IFP 20. A separate Gauteng offer, which ActionSA rejected, would have let ActionSA run Tshwane while the DA led Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni.
- [The DA secures a five-party coalition in Emfuleni after a sitting collapses](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/emfuleni.html) (South Africa, updated 24 November 2026): ANC, EFF and MK councillors disrupted Emfuleni’s mayoral election sitting, and Nova News reports it collapsed. News24 reports the DA has secured a five-party coalition to take control of the municipality, giving up posts to do so.
- [The ANC turns down ActionSA’s offer of council seats](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/pr-seats.html) (South Africa, updated 24 November 2026): The ANC won no PR seats in Gauteng’s three metros, which could keep some of its regional leaders out of council. ActionSA offered to bring ANC members in through its own lists. A senior Gauteng ANC source told The Citizen the answer is no.
- [South Africa’s cities move to coalition rule](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/i-cities.html) (International, updated 23 November 2026): Straight after the results, Bloomberg and Reuters reported that the biggest cities would be run by coalitions, and AP described high-stakes talks after the ANC’s worst result. Two weeks on, Bloomberg’s S’thembile Cele wrote that post-election bartering was counting for more than votes, while the FT and the BBC reported the ANC fighting to keep control of key cities.
- [A turning point for Mandela’s party](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/i-anc.html) (International, updated 22 November 2026): Many foreign pieces treat the result as a turning point for the ANC. The New York Times’ John Eligon wrote that South Africa’s politics may never be the same again. The Economist welcomed voters giving up on the party, AP explained how it lost its way, and the FT reported on townships turning against it.
- [What the city deals mean for the unity government](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/i-gnu.html) (International, updated 20 November 2026): Foreign outlets keep asking whether the local fights will spill into the national unity government. Bloomberg reported that the DA would stay in the GNU for now. Semafor’s Sam Mkokeli called the metros an urban test for it, Justice Malala argued in Bloomberg Opinion that the coalition government has to succeed, and Bloomberg’s Next Africa podcast asked whether it could collapse.
- [Abroad, Johannesburg is the story: a deal to shut out the DA](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/i-joburg.html) (International, updated 20 November 2026): Johannesburg gets the most attention outside South Africa. Reuters and the FT reported that the ANC and its partners were close to a deal that would sideline the DA, which won the most votes in the city. The FT reported that Helen Zille had told allies her bid for mayor was over, and The Africa Report called Herman Mashaba the kingmaker in Gauteng.
- [The rand slides as investors watch the talks](https://preamble.co.za/coalitions/i-rand.html) (International, updated 19 November 2026): Financial outlets link the talks to the currency. Reuters reported the rand at a seven-month low on 17 November as traders tracked the coalition talks, and near a one-year low two days later. Bloomberg reported it testing R17 to the dollar with the focus on politics, and Michael Cohen wrote that the messy fallout had rattled investors.
